newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico says will keep seeking ex-prosecutor.
newsitem.headline: Mexico says will keep seeking ex-prosecutor.

text.p: Mexico said Friday that it will continue to seek the deportation of ex-prosecutor Mario Ruiz Massieu from the United States after a U.S. Judge rejected a request to send him back to Mexico.

Immigration Judge Annie Sue Garcy issued a decision Friday that rejected a petition by the U.S. government to send the former deputy attorney-general back to Mexico, the Mexican government said in a statement.
The former high-level government official is wanted in Mexico on various charges, including trying to cover up a crime, torture, and money laundering.

He has been fighting a long-drawn out battle to stay out of Mexico, after being arrested on currency charges in March 1995 at Newark International Airport in New Jersey as he was about to board a plan for Spain with his wife and daughter.

He left Mexico amid charges he tried to cover up the investigation into the September 1994 assassination of his brother, Jose Francisco Ruiz Massieu, a leading member of the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI).

On Friday the Mexican Attorney-General's office said in a statement that the latest setback for it was not a definitive decision and that it will continue to search for legal means to bring Massieu to trial.
The legal battle in the United States has taken various turns.

After a U.S. district court ruled against the U.S. government's attempt to deport him in Feburary 1996, a federal appeals court last July ordered the resumption of deportation proceedings against Massieu.
On March 15 this year, he was found guilty by a federal jury in Houston, Texas, of taking millions of dollars in bribes from drug traffickers and stashing the money in a Texas bank.
In April, a U.S. district judge ruled that the U.S. government could keep all $9 million that it seized from Massieu's bank accounts, saying he got the money as bribes from drug traffickers.
The Mexican Attorney-General's office said the decision to take the $9 million from Ruiz Massieu "was not sanction enough for the actions that are attributed to him."
